summary.headline: OnMobile Q1 FY27 revenue fell 3.8% QoQ to INR 124.1 crore and EBITDA margin dropped to 1.2% as ONMO+ launch costs hit; PAT loss INR 28.9 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR 124.1 crore, down 3.8% QoQ, with mobile entertainment at INR 84.6 crore (down 6.5% QoQ) and gaming at INR 39.4 crore (up 2.4% QoQ). EBITDA was INR 1.5 crore (1.2% margin), pressured by ONMO+ launch expenses, while PAT was a loss of INR 28.9 crore including a one-time INR 14.1 crore severance charge from restructuring. ONMO+ Smart Console went live on 26 June 2026 in India, in the last four days of the quarter, and management is pursuing retail (Diwali target) and B2B operator deals. Cash fell to INR 135.5 crore after ONMO+ investment and short-term credit repayment, and a debenture issue of INR 65 crore at about 13.8% was raised.

financial_highlights.change: Lower QoQ, due to ONMO+ launch expenses
Includes one-time severance of INR 14.1 crore

segments.name: Mobile entertainment and communications (Tones, Buzzmo)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 84.6 crore, down 6.5% QoQ, driven mainly by European video service decline; management targets profitability/margin rising from about 20% to 25%. Tones is live with 27 customers.

segments.name: Mobile gaming (subscription)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 39.4 crore, up 2.4% QoQ, with 13.8 million subscribers. Marketing spend cut to below 50% of revenue (from about 65% two years ago) by pausing unprofitable accounts; target EBITDA margin 10-25% for FY27.

segments.name: ONMO+ Smart Console (new)
segments.commentary: Launched 26 June 2026 on D2C in India; no console sales volumes disclosed. Pricing cited at about $3.99/month subscription, with box revenue of $50 or $75 for 12-month pack.

guidance_outlook: Legacy mobile entertainment: aim to stop degrowth and grow 2% to 5% annually over time; margin target 20% to 25%.
Mobile gaming: target EBITDA margin of 10% to 25% this year.

ONMO+ retail: negotiating with large Indian retail groups to be in stores by Diwali (October) and Spain by October-December; India and Spain retail rollout planned for October to January, further markets February to April 2027.
Chingari investment: buy-back delayed by 12 to 18 months; valuation reassessment by year-end.
Management expects ONMO+ cash-positive after two to three years, with payback of total investment over four years.
Consolidated PAT breakeven not guided; management said it depends on how many markets launch over the next 12 to 18 months.
Potential fundraise of USD 5 million to 10 million via QIP and/or strategic investors, plus lenders and leasing.
capex_capacity: ONMO+ launch costs in Q1 are embedded in EBITDA; management declined to quantify them.
Servers and controllers require ongoing investment; server leasing rising, increasing depreciation.
Total FY27 capex not quantified; depends on the scale of market launches (low, mid, high volume plans).
Operator deals: minimum set-up of about $50K per month, possibly 2-3x with bundling; operators pay for minimum capex and boxes.
Management plans to add server points in more countries as ONMO+ expands.
demand_pricing: ONMO+ usage: 70 minutes per subscriber, about 2x top-10% PC median; D7 vs D30 retention 2.7x industry; 82% of users under 35.
Sessions split: desktop 44%, TV 31%; 75% of users have tried more than five games.
Smart Console operator pipeline: about 20 international operators or broadband providers in discussion, 10 in commercial discussion; 2-3 commercial proposals per week.
Mobile entertainment: four or five significant platform deals under discussion; Buzzmo deal near signing; Viasat and Gameye deals in progress.
Competitors cited: Xbox xCloud and NVIDIA GeForce Now; management claims ONMO+ pricing is about half of competitors' cost.
Gaming subscription: more than 50 live accounts reviewed; some paused on weak return on ad spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why is subscription gaming revenue falling for two quarters, and is the 2 million MRR target still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management paused accounts with weak return on ad spend across more than 50 live accounts; reaching 2 million MRR may take three to four quarters, not guaranteed.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery of about INR 45 crore owed by DeOSphere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the amount must be settled within the next two quarters; no detail on the recovery route was given.

qa_highlights.question: Severance of INR 14.1 crore looks high versus salaries of INR 22 crore; which team was downsized?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the INR 14.1 crore is a full-year figure covering India and international, with some European severance reaching two years' salary. Spain labour rules were cited as a driver.

qa_highlights.question: Manpower cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: People costs to remain at 20% to 22% of revenue, though ONMO+ hiring may add headcount.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise INR 65 crore debt at about 13.8% with INR 135.5 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt funds ONMO+ and repays short-term facilities; part of cash sits in geographies with transfer restrictions.

qa_highlights.question: Is a QIP planned, and at what size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fundraise should be USD 5 million to 10 million, combining QIP and strategic investors; current valuation seen as too low.

risks_watch: Low EBITDA margin (1.2%) and PAT loss; ONMO+ launch costs and servers will weigh further on EBITDA and depreciation.
Funding need is not sized; fundraise and borrowing at about 13.8% add financial risk.
Chingari investment valuation not reassessed until year-end; possible future provisioning.
DeOSphere receivable (about INR 45 crore written off) to be resolved within two quarters.
Retail launch timing (Diwali target) and store execution; management says connectivity-related customer reviews are a risk.
Continued European video revenue decline in mobile entertainment; Vodafone business still under discussion.
Management has said it will not disclose ONMO+ sales or PO volumes going forward.
summary.management_tone: Confident about the ONMO+ product and early usage data, but cautious on financials: management said the quarter was weak due to restructuring and launch costs and asked investors to judge performance annually. Answers on ONMO+ sales volumes, capex size, and PAT timing were evasive, and management deferred most of these to future quarters.

So, it's a very big step forward that we took going live.
Obviously, we're a public company, and I want to share this information with you so that you at least confirm that, we have a good service.
So the revenue range is quite high at $50 a box or $75 when you take the 12-month pack.

adds.what: ONMO+ Smart Console server points and retail rollout in India and Spain (no console volumes or box count disclosed)

growth.why: No consolidated revenue growth guidance; legacy mobile entertainment targets 2-5% annual growth "eventually" while Q1 revenue fell 3.8% QoQ, and ONMO+ retail/operator deals (Diwali target, ~20 operators in discussion, no signed volumes) are not yet backed by firm orders, and the company says further aggressive expansion needs fresh fundraising.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to 1.2% on ONMO+ launch costs, but gaming target EBITDA margin of 10-25% this year and legacy 20-25% target, with marketing cut to below 50% of revenue from about 65% two years ago, point to recovery only if ONMO+ costs stop rising and paused accounts stay out.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ONMO+ server points are being added in more countries and retail rollout in India and Spain is planned for October to January, with further markets February to April 2027, though no console volumes or capex size were disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 revenue fell 3.8% QoQ (mobile entertainment down 6.5%), gaming subscription revenue fell for two quarters, and 2 million MRR may take three to four quarters; ONMO+ volumes are undisclosed and operator deals are not yet signed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says India and Spain budgets are covered, and further aggressive expansion requires fresh fundraising of USD 5-10 million, so a larger capex plan depends on raising money.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue fell 3.8% QoQ, PAT loss of INR 28.9 crore and consolidated PAT breakeven is not guided, and the gaming MRR target was pushed out to three to four quarters.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gaming MRR target of 2 million per month cut to a three-to-four-quarter horizon, Chingari buy-back delayed 12-18 months with valuation review at year-end, and the INR 45 crore DeOSphere recovery is unresolved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ONMO+ retail in Indian stores targeted for Diwali (October), Spain by October-December, and Buzzmo deal near signing with Viasat and Gameye deals in progress, though none is firmly dated.

rows.label: Operator deals for ONMO+ Smart Console
rows.why: About 20 international operators in discussion, 10 in commercial talks and 2-3 commercial proposals per week, with minimum set-up of about $50K per month, but no signed volumes disclosed.

rows.label: Debt-funded cash burn and fundraise
rows.why: Cash fell to INR 135.5 crore, INR 65 crore debenture raised at about 13.8%, and a USD 5-10 million QIP or strategic raise is being pursued.

rows.label: DSO improvement
rows.why: DSO fell 10 days to 121 days, but the INR 45 crore DeOSphere receivable must be settled within two quarters and its recovery route is not yet known.

tone.note: Management was confident about ONMO+ product and early usage (70 minutes per subscriber, D7 retention 2.7x industry) but cautious on financials and evasive on ONMO+ volumes, capex size and PAT timing; analysts pressed on gaming subscription decline, the INR 14.1 crore severance, the 13.8% debt raise
